items.excerpt: iZotope leaves Native Instruments (sold to inMusic in May 2026) and joins founder-owned Boris FX, which cites iZotope's 'smart and practical use of AI' in RX/Ozone as the reason for the pairing; all existing licenses and plugin development continue uninterrupted. Follows the just-published RX12 review card, so this is the industry follow-up beat. (Date from MusicTech byline '3 days ago' at fetch on 2026-07-06; de-duped against CDM 07-02, Sound On Sound 07-02 and Bedroom Producers Blog 07-03 coverage — MusicTech kept for the clearest AI rationale quotes.)

Booking agency Good Intent apologised after unknowingly putting AI-generated 'artist' Afro Charles on the bill of a July 1 Sydney live show; the act's reps had pitched it as a 'producer' with 'live vocals', and musician Aidan Sammut exposed the deception. Agency and venue Bootleggers promise tougher vetting and a Support Act donation — a first-of-its-kind AI-slop-hits-the-stage story. (On-page timestamp: July 3, 2026, 2:27 PM.)

MusicRadar goes inside ChatDSP, Amorph and Pluginmaker.ai — three new 'vibe coding' platforms that turn natural-language prompts into working audio plugins with zero C++/DSP knowledge, with makers claiming manual coding 'won't be a thing' in a few years, plus pushback on environmental cost and developer jobs. Distinct from the published Sugar Bytes DrumComputer-Claude card (that was one plugin gaining a text interface; this is prompt-to-plugin generation). (Dated June 26, 2026 on page.)

Steinberg ships SpectraLayers 13: AI-powered Unmix Sound Effects pulls incidental sounds out of ambience, generative Ambience Heal fills the holes left behind, and a Voice Enhance module uses generative AI to rebuild badly recorded speech, alongside Unmix Two Voices, DeCrosstalk and Dolby Atmos round-tripping. (SOS listing date 2/7/26 = 2 July 2026; Gearnews covered the same release 03 Jul — de-duped, SOS kept as primary source.)
